{
  "verdict": "revise",
  "score": 0.58,
  "reasons": [
    "Time-series section is incomplete: only the 2022 entry (fraunhofer-47.6-2022) is shown; missing subsequent top-record entries (2023-2025) required by the brief.",
    "Explicitly requested: (a) current best by category for lab single-junction, lab multi-junction, and commercial module. The artifact notes 'No explicit single-junction' and 'No commercial-module records' but does not clearly present a finalized, publishable summary with explicit values across all three categories.",
    "(c) is not fully addressed: while a mention of the Shockley–Queisser limit appears, there is no structured, quantified comparison of measured records to the theoretical limits nor a dedicated section/chart for this comparison.",
    "Deliverable format guidance (efficiency_analysis.md with tables, short charts, links, and a CSV appendix) is not fully satisfied: the artifact is a textual summary/table and does not include the Markdown file layout, chart descriptions, or an attached CSV appendix."
  ],
  "guidance": "Produce a complete efficiency_analysis.md that (a) lists current best reported efficiencies by category with explicit values (lab single-junction, lab multi-junction, commercial module) or state clearly when a category has no records in the ingested data; (b) presents a simple time-series of record improvements for the three categories, with year, id, efficiency, and source; (c) adds a quantified comparison to theoretical limits (e.g., Shockley–Queisser ~33.7% for single-junction) and discusses gaps for multi-junction limits; (d) normalizes all efficiencies to two decimals, labels devices as 'cell' or 'module', and notes test conditions; (e) includes a small CSV appendix (e.g., appendix.csv) with the normalized records (id, date, device_label, category, efficiency_pct, spectrum, concentration_suns, temperature_C, source_url); (f) embeds links back to original sources in the markdown; (g) saves as efficiency_analysis.md and ensures the content is publication-ready. Use the ingested dataset as the source of truth, and clearly separate confirmed data from caveats."
}
